active_inquiry.closure_condition: Close when trajectory evidence from a trained candidate distinguishes the dominant mechanism with first-entry time, post-entry excursions, endpoint speed, longest uninterrupted in-band run, branch and joint-limit behavior, and target-geometry stratification, and supports a specific next intervention or shows that no credible route remains.
active_inquiry.goal_connection: Identifying the dominant failure mechanism directly determines whether the campaign should improve target-conditioned transport and branch selection or develop a braking and stabilization route toward at least 196 complete holds in the 200-episode official assessment.
active_inquiry.question: Under the first credible learned-control route, is the dominant limit on complete-hold success failure to transport and select a viable inverse-kinematic branch, or failure after first entry caused by residual velocity, braking, boundary excursions, or stabilization, and how does that mechanism vary across target radius and angle?
active_inquiry.rationale: The physical model establishes nominal reachability but provides no candidate or trajectory evidence. Official assessment is unavailable without an explicit best-known candidate, and a no-route conclusion is unsupported. A bounded trajectory-level inquiry is therefore the most goal-relevant action.
